analysis: Reviewed three files in this PR. (1) SchedulerPrefillBenchmark.swift: schema bumped to 5, adding prefillChunkTokens and maxBatchedTokensPerStep, with geometry read via EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry. This is benchmark-only and touches no network, key, attestation or cache surface. Report fields are optional, so old payloads still decode. (2) SchedulerPrefillDecisionLiveRunner.swift: the new engineEnvironment helper overrides chunk, step-budget, stripe and max-partial-prefill keys on a copied environment dictionary. It is used only for benchmark construction (constructionPurpose .benchmark), with no production path. (3) EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift: this is the one production-relevant change. Wide prefill chunk (2048) is now the default for GPT-OSS, dense Qwen3.5 and Gemma4, and new env overrides DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS are added. Both overrides are operator-local environment settings, so they sit in the operator's own control domain and give no new remote or consumer-reachable attack surface. Parsing fails safe to SDK defaults on malformed, zero or negative values. Step budget doubling uses multipliedReportingOverflow. An explicit very large chunk value is accepted without an upper bound, but the operator already controls the process and can sabotage its own availability (T-016/T-003 class), so this is not a regression. bidirectionalMediaPrefillChunkCeiling keeps the SDK chunk for media requests. Larger chunks raise transient activation memory, which is an availability/performance matter (T-029/T-010 class) and is not shown to be a security regression. The prefix-cache (T-041) scope is unchanged: no change to SSD cache keys, TTL, salt, or gating is visible. The diff does not show whether the cache block size interacts with the new chunk geometry (block alignment, paged pool sizing). The prefillGeometry-sized paged pool code and the CBv2 scheduler consumers are outside the supplied evidence. No findings.
